reviews.text:
Simple and effective. I love the simple and lovely design of this app. It’s ease of use makes it a no-brainer. I had the app for about a week before I realized that this could revolutionize my life, and I did end up buying the lifetime membership. Now I’ve had it for about a month and I couldn’t be happier. 
I use it as a daily to-do for house cleaning. Every day I have the habits “put a load of laundry in” and “fold yesterday’s laundry and put away.” I have load the dishwasher in the evening and put dishes away before work in the morning. And then I made a series of “weekly habits” to spend 30 minutes each day on a different room in the house. 
And it’s working. Sure I don’t get to the laundry every day. But even with a little inconsistency my laundry pile shrinks more than it grows. That’s the mind blowing thing, I’m watching my little avocado plant grow, and my house, while far from spotless, is starting to feel more like a home and less like a noose. This app is a gentle positive reminder of what I want to accomplish, and frankly that’s exactly what I needed.

reviews.text:
Okay can you What I Was Looking For. I’ve spent a lot of time trying to find a habit tracker / routine app, and most of the apps I’ve tried so far have a lot of complexity, aren’t customizable enough for what I’m looking for, or aren’t aesthetic enough for me to enjoy using. The closest I got was using the regular notes app on iPhone

With this app, it’s super simple, I can organize routines by time of day, or add habits not related to time of day. It’s also pretty, and was super easy for me to use as opposed to the notes app. I don’t get drawn into the app and end up spending more time using it than actually doing my habits, which has been way more helpful to me than apps that reward time spent in the app.

The plant is cute and nice, and habits can be tracked individually or as groups. There’s no punishment for not completing tasks, and the plant grows every time you complete one habit per day, not all habits. It’s very rewarding for people who may be trying to build multiple habits as well as those building one habit at a time. It offers suggestion while also giving you a lot of autonomy in building habits.

All around, this is by far my favorite and most helpful app I currently have on my phone due to its impacts on my real life. In the future, I would love to see some optimization in habits we are trying to quit while keeping the shame free environment it currently has.

A huge thank you to the developers for making an app that I’ve actively been looking for for so long 💕

reviews.text:
LOVE! Visually pleasing, user friendly!. I literally downloaded 30 different habit/productivity/tracker apps on my phone to see which would work for me, and this is the only one that came remotely close to meeting my needs. I would open each app and enter in a few habits/items, and pretty instantly knew which ones would not work. Everyone has different needs, but here were
MY NEEDS MET:
1. View my list as soon as I open the app, not have to navigate through the app to find it
2. See my daily/weekly repeat tasks & habits specifically in bubbles or circles, NOT in list form. So I can fit more items in one space next to each other (as in same priority)
3. Colorful & customizable, but with colors that complement each other, not clash
4. Pictures, emojis, symbols… anything to help represent the words/ideas/habits on the list

BONUS: Besides being absolutely adorable and welcoming, Avocation was by far the most user-friendly - easiest to input habits/items, and your items for the day are the first thing that show up when you open the app (which was not the case for many of the other apps I instantly deleted)!!!
 I am very visually oriented, I always add emojis to any list on my phone, shopping, calendar, to do, etc. so I greatly appreciate having pictures along side items, a bunch of categories to label your item and 12 colors if you need to further categorize like I do. It is SO crucial to be able to go back and edit items, be it the days of the week/frequency, color categorization, words used to describe the habit or item. you can even categorize time of day: any time, morning, afternoon, evening.

WOULD LOVE TO SEE IN THE FUTURE:
1. A calendar view of upcoming habits, or being able to tap a day on the calendar and see what the list of habits is for that day.
2. Having a biweekly or monthly (as in once a month habit) option. Like washing house windows and other big projects that don’t need to be done every week
3. An “information“ page to look at in settings. Sorry! Just to for me to refer back to, especially right now in the beginning as I’m deep diving this app, so I remember what it is that I am looking at. Or, for example, an option to tap on the water jug, and it tells me that it is so much percent full, and what filling the jar with water does. 

If I could, I would a billion percent replace my regular calendar with this app! Love it entirely!! thank you so much!

So cute & easy to use!. I’m definitely one of those people that need to write a list every day of things to accomplish or I’ll end up sitting on the couch all day. I often times made lists that were lengthy and unorganized which resulted in me feeling overwhelmed or discouraged when I didn’t finish everything. So I went on the hunt for an app to help motivate me and this app is exactly what I’ve been looking for!

Not only is this app super cute, it’s so easy to use! I love the simplicity of it and how customizable it is to fit everyone’s unique tasks, goals or habits as they came them in the app. I tried a few other apps and in comparison I found that Avocation really motivated me to stay on track and organize my daily habits so I can accomplish them easily. Plus, the cute characters make it fun! My favorite thing about the app is the creative freedom they give by letting you customize your habit entirely with your own title, color, days of the week and time of day.

I would highly recommend! You can download the app for free to try it out and see how you like it. It limits how much you can do in the free experience but honesty, it’s worth the $10 (one time purchase for lifetime benefits) to not only get all the features of this beautiful app but also support the creators who clearly are making this app to help others. A one time payment for all the benefits of the app?? It’s very affordable and generous of the creators! Most apps I tried will charge you monthly or yearly!

One suggestion I’d like to make: It would be awesome if the habits were organizable! I love that they are separated by morning, afternoon and evening but currently the habits in each section stay in order by creation. So it would be nice to have a filter option to sort them by specific time, type of habit or importance or to be able to drag the habit bubbles to be in a custom desired order.

reviews.text: Hidden Treasure. I had my doubts about this application because it did not have a lot of reviews. I usually go for the stuff that many other people have tried. I was coming from using one of the most popular habit forming applications available and not being very satisfied. I loved the graphics instantly. I am a very visual person and this made a huge difference in my mind from the start. I used it a few minutes and took a chance: I purchased the lifetime membership. It has been a couple of weeks, and I know now that I made a great decision. This application is life changing if you allow it to become that. Even though it is a bit more expensive, I love the honesty of a pricier lifetime membership versus the subscription model that so many “extortionists” are using now for their own half baked applications. As you complete habits, you water a plant that grows into a tree. What a beautiful, creative, and almost poetic concept. I absolutely love it and took the time to write this long thank you letter to whoever decided to create this beautiful application. May you be happy, loved, and successful.

reviews.text:
This app is making me a better version of myself. I honestly love this app. I’ve tried other task management apps in the past (i.e. Evernote, Google Calendar), but generally don’t stick to using those after a few days. 

This app is different.

It has a VERY cute, clean design. Other apps feel overwhelming just looking at them (they’re usually cluttered with lists, graphs, and other features that can be anxiety producing). Avocation is minimalist, without being boring. The circles used to track your habits are actually kind of soothing to look at and the icons are so clever and sleek. 

This is the first time I’ve consistently stuck with a lot of my daily personal goals that I’ve struggled with in the past (drinking more water, stretching, sticking to a skin care routine, etc.)

Unlike other apps, this gives you a motivation outside of finishing a goal for yourself, which you just need sometimes. In all honesty, the idea that completing a task will grow a virtual plant is so motivating. No other task/habit app has that. I love it! Growing my plant has 100% been the thing that has kept me on track. 

There’s only a few things I would hope for in the future and those are: a calendar to track progress (no graphs or anything, just where you can open it to a day and see what happened or how full you get the water jug any given day), the ability to make edits for/see something more than a day old (if you forgot to check a task off), and more plant pot options. 

TL,DR This app is awesome. Sleek. Simple. Effective. Perfect layout/design. Motivates you with cute icons and a plant you grow when you get stuff done!
